key_insight: The paper shows that decentralized online Riemannian optimization can achieve the optimal $O(\log T)$ regret for strongly geodesically convex losses by combining time-varying step-size analysis with new network-error bounds.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable learning and control on curved state spaces in distributed systems, including settings such as consensus, sensing, and robotics on manifolds with positive curvature.
method: Derive a general network-error analysis for decentralized Riemannian optimization with time-varying step sizes.
Use the analysis to prove $O(\log T)$ static regret for decentralized online Riemannian gradient descent.
Extend the result to two-point bandit feedback via strong subconvexity of smoothed losses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical regret guarantees, including the first decentralized $O(\log T)$ bound for strongly g-convex losses and the same rate under two-point bandit feedback.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on bounded sectional curvature and carefully decaying step sizes, so practical performance may be sensitive to manifold geometry, network connectivity, and parameter tuning.
paper_title: Decentralized Online Riemannian Optimization for Strongly Geodesically Convex Functions
